item.title: A thin carbon membrane to capture carbon
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01960-2

Anthropogenic emissions are rapidly increasing atmospheric CO2 levels, with severe consequences for the global climate. Researchers have developed a carbon membrane as thin as only two molecular layers that sieves and captures CO2 with very high flux and selectivity, holding promise for climate change mitigation technologies.
item.dc:title: A thin carbon membrane to capture carbon
item.dc:creator: Alexander Knebel

item.title: Recyclable flow battery chemistry
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01979-5

Turning water-based flow batteries into a truly sustainable technology hinges on recycling the organic molecules inside the battery. A redox-active organic molecule has now been developed that not only outperforms the industry-standard vanadium benchmark but also offers exceptional reusability.
item.dc:title: Recyclable flow battery chemistry
item.dc:creator: Sungmin Park
Yongchai Kwon

item.title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01970-0

Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance.
item.dc:title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries

item.title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01973-x

Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO2 separation.
